description: With the offset at the cap the occupant dials the thermostat to 73 F. The real coordinator confirms an override; for the whole override the bedroom swings through both sides of the hysteresis band and CA writes NOTHING; the occupant's value stays. When the manual grace ends, CA re-asserts the plain 66 F (offset forgotten).

events.note: The hallway thermostat's own sensor: satisfied, so it will not start by itself.
Day classification (cold: heat all night / hot: cool all night).
Bedtime: the sleep band is written and the sleep window (remote sensor in use) begins.
The occupant dials the thermostat to 73 F (the furnace is idle).
Bedroom swings past target + swing (66 + 1.5): a step-down would be due.
Bedroom back far below target: a raise would be due.
After the override's grace ended: the bedroom is still far below target.

assertions.reason: Precondition: CA's offset is at the +4 F cap when the occupant turns the dial.
The occupant's dial to 73 F was detected and confirmed as an override by the real coordinator.
From the dial until the override ends CA writes NOTHING, though the bedroom swings through both sides of the hysteresis band: the occupant's 73 F stays.

notes: Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md section 10), Issue #1194 increment (e). Tier A: the real ClimateAdvisorCoordinator + AutomationEngine under FakeHass/FakeScheduler (use_coordinator=true, so the sleep-sensor listener and the 1-minute timer are real); every assertion is track=integration for that reason and is evaluated, not skipped.

(a) Effectiveness: scratch-copy mutation run of this scenario against the production code (worktree untouched). It FAILS when M01: the whole offset deleted (the write path adds 0 and the check is a no-op); M02: the +4 F cap removed; M05: the whole gate predicate deleted (always PROCEED); M13: the override terms removed from the gate. Passes unmutated.

(b) Docs <-> production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md 'Remote-sensor outer loop on the thermostat setpoint (Issue #1194, increment a)': 'Gates' override rows and 'Occupant change with an offset applied'. Matches production.
(c) Occupant outcome if this regressed: A person who turns the dial must not have the loop silently move it a minute later.

verdict.summary: The occupant's own setpoint wins; CA does not step over it.
verdict.observed_behavior: No CA set_temperature from the dial (21:20) until the grace expiry (21:37:00); then the plain 66 F.
verdict.expected_behavior: Loop silent through pending and confirmed phases.
